title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No outright error. The question 1⊗X ≅ X is (correctly) left open: with only 'weak' representability of bilinear and degree-0 maps it does not follow, which Grothendieck himself recognizes on the next page by introducing 'bon' (stable under composition) tensor products.
The transcription's 's_{X⊗Y}·s_{Y⊗X} = id_{Y⊗X}' should read s_{X,Y}∘s_{Y,X} = id_{Y⊗X}; as written in the transcription it is meaningless.

The claim that Γ^n X is functorial in X 'dans P_1' is fine; functoriality for polynomial maps of X would require compatibility of composition with degrees (axiom e). This is implicitly available but not stated.

ideas.what: Tensor product defined as the object representing bidegree-(1,1) (bilinear) maps in a multicategory-like 'polynomial structure'; symmetry from the permutation axiom
ideas.modern_name: Representable (symmetric) multicategory; tensor product as representing object of multimorphisms
ideas.where_published: Universal bilinear maps appear routinely (e.g. EGA 0 / SGA 4 style), but not this axiomatic multicategorical setting as far as I know

ideas.what: Γ^n X defined as the object representing homogeneous degree-n polynomial maps out of X; Γ^0 = 𝟙 representing constants via the axiom that constant maps are independent of the source
ideas.modern_name: Divided powers as universal for polynomial laws (Roby); categorical form close to the Γ^d-categories of strict polynomial functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (1963) for modules; Friedlander–Suslin (1997) for the Γ^d P category; later Kuhn, Touzé, Krause

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'structure polynomiale' on an additive category: multidegree-graded polynomial maps with composition, degree rule, weight decomposition, symmetry and constants; the tensor product and Γ^n are derived from it by representability
ideas.modern_name: Graded/polynomial enrichment of an additive category; a 'polynomial multicategory' (no standard name)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No single standard source; related to strict polynomial functor theory (Friedlander–Suslin) and to polynomial laws (Roby)

ideas.what: Question whether the unit 𝟙 = Γ^0 automatically satisfies 𝟙⊗X ≅ X, leading (next page) to the notion of 'bon produit tensoriel' (universal property stable under further composition)
ideas.modern_name: Strong/'closed under composition' representability in representable multicategories, which yields unit and associativity constraints

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds a single axiomatic framework, an additive category with multidegree-graded polynomial maps, in which both the tensor product (from bilinear maps) and divided powers Γ^n (from homogeneous degree-n maps) arise as representing objects, with the unit as Γ^0. This merges the representable-multicategory view of monoidal structure with Roby's polynomial laws. The literature treats these separately: Hermida for multicategories; Roby and Friedlander–Suslin for Γ^d. A unified 'polynomial multicategory' in which ⊗ and Γ^n are both universal does not seem standard.
missed.quote: Si, pour X,Y fixés, Z variable, ce foncteur est représentable, l'objet qui le représente est noté X⊗Y ... si le foncteur Y ↦ P_n(X,Y) sur P_1 est représentable, l'objet qui le représente est noté Γ^n X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Strict polynomial functors, divided power structures in derived and spectral algebraic geometry, and polynomial monads would benefit from a multicategorical axiomatization where Γ and ⊗ are universal objects. This would give coherence (unit, associativity, Γ^a⊗Γ^b → Γ^{a+b}) for free from a 'good representability' condition.

missed.claim: The question whether 𝟙 = Γ^0 is automatically a unit for ⊗ (𝟙⊗X ≅ X, 𝟙⊗𝟙 ≅ 𝟙) is posed but answered only by strengthening the axioms ('bon produit tensoriel' on the next page). The precise minimal conditions under which a polynomial structure yields a symmetric monoidal category with compatible Γ-structure appear unworked-out.
missed.quote: Peut-on dire que si 𝟙 existe, alors ∀X ∈ Ob P, 𝟙⊗X ≃ X i.e. P_(1,1)(𝟙,X;Y) ≃ P_1(X,Y) ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precise coherence question for polynomial (non-additive) enrichments, relevant to axiomatizing Γ- and λ-operations on perfect complexes and in K-theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual ingredients are known: universal bilinear maps, and divided powers representing polynomial laws (Roby 1963). The interest is Grothendieck's axiomatic 'polynomial structure' producing both ⊗ and Γ^n by representability. His recognition (with the next page) that a strengthened, composition-stable representability is needed for unit and coherence anticipates Hermida's 2000 representable multicategories in a polynomial setting. This is a notable unpublished framework but not a finished uncredited theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'La donnée d'une st.[?] polynomiale' → 'La donnée d'une structure polynomiale P'.
'(et de même avec plus d'arguments [?] 2 gauches[?])' → likely '(et de même avec plus d'arguments à gauche)'.
'mais on peut X,Y [...] considérer comme dans P!' → roughly '(mais on peut prendre X,Y variables comme objets dans P !)', i.e. functoriality also for polynomial maps.
'ils sont can. isomorphes [...] s_{X,Y})' → 'ils sont can. isomorphes (iso noté s_{X,Y})'.
'L'objet Γ^0(X) existe ssi P^o(0) existe' → most likely 'ssi Γ^0(0) existe' (by axiom g, Γ^0(X) = Γ^0(0)).
